task:
MARK THE GUIDE'S COLONY-TYPE PORTS SO THEY TAKE THEIR BODY'S ECONOMY, AND SEPARATE "THE COLONY SHIP" FROM "COLONY-TYPE PORT".

Context: in apps/api/src/domain/facility_catalogue_v1.json only the colony_ship bootstrap entry has is_colony_port true, because apps/importer/src/import_facility_templates_from_daftmav.py hard-codes 'is_colony_port': False for every DaftMav row. So a Coriolis, Orbis etc. never inherits its body's economy and the simulator shows it as "Colony 2.0". The Elite Dangerous Colonization Mega Guide v2.3.0 (PDF p7 definitions and p48 table) says colony-type ports are the ports whose economy type is "Colony": Civilian and Commercial space outposts, Coriolis, Orbis, Ocellus, the Civilian planetary outpost and the Tier 3 planetary port; all other ports (Asteroid Base, Industrial/Criminal/Military/Scientific space outposts, Industrial/Scientific planetary outposts) are specialised and keep their own economy. Raven Colonial (ravencolonial.com, src/site-data.ts) gives the Dodec starport economy "colony" too. This catalogue feeds only the planner/simulation code; it is NOT used by Ratings V4, the published Finder products, shared_contracts/ or apps/web/ - do not touch those.

Required changes:
1. Importer: set is_colony_port = is_port and economy == 'Colony' for DaftMav rows (the guide's own definition). Regenerate facility_catalogue_v1.json through the importer functions exactly as the existing regeneration test in tests/test_import_facility_templates_from_daftmav.py requires (same serialisation and order). Only is_colony_port may change. Expected: exactly these 8 entries change false -> true: orbital_outpost_civilian, orbital_outpost_commercial, coriolis_station, orbis_t3, ocellus_station, dodecahedron_t3 (comment: not named in guide v2.3.0; Raven Colonial lists it as colony), surface_planetary_port_outpost_civilian, planetary_port. colony_ship stays true; every other entry stays false.
2. Several call sites use is_colony_port to mean "the bootstrap colony ship". After step 1 that would wrongly exclude Coriolis/Orbis etc. Add one small helper for the colony ship (for example is_colony_ship(template) in apps/api/src/domain/facilities.py, true only for the bootstrap entry id 'colony_ship') and use it at the colony-ship call sites: optimiser/candidate_generator.py _is_useful_candidate, optimiser/facility_selection.py select_port_template, optimiser/guided_planner.py _select_port, simulation/buildability.py _select_facilities_for_archetype ("Always include colony ship"). Keep is_colony_port at the economy call sites: simulation/build_preview.py (_placement_economy_profile, _economy_weight), simulation/port_economy.py _economy_weight, simulation/composition.py _economy_weight, simulation/economy_simulator.py _economy_weight, optimiser/plan_quality.py _economy_counts. Grep for every other is_colony_port use and state in your summary which group each belongs to.
3. Do not change economy weights (colony 1.2, specialised 2.0, support 1.0 stay as they are; a separate change will fix them), costs, tiers, is_port, API response shapes, field names or OpenAPI output; do not edit Ratings V4 files, shared_contracts/, sql/, apps/web/ or frontend/.

Tests (pytest, no database):
(a) Catalogue/importer: the 8 ids above have is_colony_port true; asteroid_base, orbital_outpost_industrial, orbital_outpost_criminal, orbital_outpost_military, orbital_outpost_scientific, surface_planetary_port_outpost_industrial and surface_planetary_port_outpost_scientific are false; exactly 8 entries differ from the previous catalogue; the existing regeneration test still passes unchanged in intent.
(b) Behaviour with the bundled catalogue via simulate_build_preview and a body profile {'base_economies': ['Refinery'], 'subtype': 'rocky body'}: each of coriolis_station, orbis_t3, ocellus_station, dodecahedron_t3, orbital_outpost_civilian, orbital_outpost_commercial, planetary_port and surface_planetary_port_outpost_civilian placed alone as primary port has final_economy_strengths {'Refinery': 1.2} (same as colony_ship; previously {'Colony': 2.0}); asteroid_base stays {'Extraction': 2.0} and orbital_outpost_industrial stays {'Industrial': 2.0}. A Coriolis on an Earth-like body profile (base Tourism, HighTech, Agriculture, Military; tag elw_mixed) gets body_inheritance ledger rows for exactly those four economies.
(c) Pass-through: surface_planetary_port_outpost_civilian as primary port with a coriolis_station on the same rocky Refinery body gives a pass_through ledger entry of Refinery 0.4 and Coriolis final {'Refinery': 1.6}; with planetary_port instead it is Refinery 1.2 and Coriolis final {'Refinery': 2.4} (previously both passed 'Colony').
(d) Colony-ship separation, behaviour preserved: with the bundled catalogue, select_port_template returns the same ids as before for every strategy: primary_port_bootstrap -> orbital_outpost_civilian, low_cp -> orbital_outpost_civilian, services_aware -> asteroid_base, balanced -> asteroid_base, balanced_expansion -> asteroid_base, support_body -> asteroid_base, main_station -> planetary_port, industrial_refinery -> orbital_outpost_civilian, tourism_agriculture -> orbital_outpost_civilian; guided_planner._select_port returns light -> orbital_outpost_civilian, balanced -> asteroid_base, maxed -> planetary_port; buildability._select_facilities_for_archetype still puts exactly colony_ship (not another colony-type port) first; _is_useful_candidate still rejects a candidate whose only known template is colony_ship.
Update existing tests that pinned 'Colony' economies for these ports so they assert the new contract; never delete or weaken an assertion just to make it pass; explain each test change in your summary. Run ruff on touched files and pytest on every test file that imports the facilities domain, the bundled catalogue, the importer, build_preview, port_economy, composition, economy_simulator, buildability, the optimiser or recommendations. In your summary list every changed catalogue entry and every changed call site.
